prompt: You must recommend whether the board should divest a non-core business unit. Write the storyline, leading with the recommendation.
context: The unit generates $18M revenue/year (4% of company total) at an 11% operating margin, roughly in line with the corporate average. It requires disproportionate management attention: the CEO estimates roughly 20% of the executive team's time goes to this unit despite its 4% revenue contribution. Three potential acquirers have expressed informal interest (unsolicited) in the past year. No formal valuation or sale process has been run yet.

binaryCriteria.description: Does not claim the unit is a financial underperformer on margin, since the context states its margin (11%) is roughly in line with the corporate average.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the answer justifies divestiture primarily on the basis of poor margin/profitability.

binaryCriteria.description: Uses the mismatch between 4% revenue contribution and 20% of executive attention as the central strategic rationale.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if this specific opportunity-cost argument is absent from the storyline.

binaryCriteria.description: Recommends running a formal sale/valuation process rather than asserting a specific sale outcome or price, since none has been established yet.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the answer asserts a specific valuation or guarantees a sale will happen, rather than recommending a process to test the market.

goldNotes: A strong storyline leads with a recommendation to explore a sale process (not a flat "divest now" or "keep forever" claim, since no valuation exists yet — the honest recommendation is to run a process to find out), and should explicitly note the mismatch between the unit's 4% revenue contribution and its 20% share of executive attention as the central strategic argument (a real opportunity-cost problem, not primarily a financial-performance problem, since the unit's margin is in line with the corporate average, not underperforming). It should treat the unsolicited acquirer interest as a signal worth testing via a process, not as a reason to skip valuation and accept an assumed price. A weak answer treats this as a straightforward "sell because margin is bad" case — that framing is not supported by the data (margin is in line with the average) and would be a factual misuse of the context.
